meta.note: Seed scenarios written from the case facts in the PRD. They need approval before go-live (open question 8: who approves the Trust Challenge scenarios).

dimensions.label: Credibility
dimensions.help: Knows the facts, says what is true, admits what is not known yet.

dimensions.label: Reliability
dimensions.help: Commits only to what can be delivered and links back to earlier promises.

dimensions.label: Closeness
dimensions.help: Makes it safe to raise worries and listens to what matters to the client.

dimensions.label: Low self-interest
dimensions.help: Puts the client's outcome ahead of the bank's convenience or targets.

sittings.title: The promise check
sittings.scenario: Nadia calls one to one. She has her written log of the bank's promises open and wants to go through what has been kept, what has slipped and why.
sittings.opening: I have my log open. Before we talk about anything new, tell me which of your promises are done, which are not, and why.

sittings.title: The shortcut
sittings.scenario: Nadia is under pressure from her own board. She asks whether the bank could release one urgent payment with a single approver, just this once, while the other signatories are still being registered.
sittings.opening: I need a favour. One urgent payment, one approver, just this once. Can you make that happen today?

sittings.title: The worry behind the question
sittings.scenario: Nadia sounds tired. She asks a routine question about cut-off times, but it is clear something else is worrying her about how the change of bank is landing with her team.
sittings.opening: Quick one. What is the cut-off again for tomorrow's file? Sorry, it has been a long week.
